text: Town of Boxborough Massachusetts OFFICIAL WARRANT SPECIAL TOWN MEETING Monday, March 9, 2026 – 7:00 PM Voter check-in begins at 6:30 PM Blanchard Memorial School Gymnasium 493 Massachusetts Avenue, Boxborough Please bring this Warrant with you to the Special Town Meeting Free On-Site Child Care 6:30–9:00 PM Sign up with QR code on page 3 Special Town Election-Related to Articles 1 and 2 March 17, 2026 7:00 AM – 8:00 PM Town Hall, 29 Middle Road 1 TABLE OF CONTENTS ARTICLE 1 PURCHASE OF PROPERTY AT 984 MASSACHUSETTS AVENUE FOR NEW FIREHOUSE... 4 ARTICLE 2 NEW FIREHOUSE DESIGN & BID FUNDING ... 9 ARTICLE 3 FIREHOUSE LAND AQUISITION: RELATED COSTS ... 144 2 TOWN OF BOXBOROUGH SPECIAL TOWN MEETING Monday, March 9, 2026 7:00 PM To either of the Constables of the Town of Boxborough, Greetings: In the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, you are hereby required to notify all residents of the Town of Boxborough, who shall be qualified to vote in accordance with the provisions of MGL Chapter 51, Section 1, to meet at the Blanchard Memorial School, 493 Massachusetts Avenue, Boxborough, MA starting on Monday, March 9, 2026 at 7:00 PM, to act on Articles 1 through 3 of this Special Town Meeting Warrant. 3 Dennis Reip, Town Moderator called the Special Town Meeting to order at 7:03 pm. A total of 334 registered voters attended. Robert Stemple, Select Board member, led the pledge of allegiance. Moderator Reip introduced the Town Clerk, Town Counsel, Town Administrator Michael Johns and the Select Board: Chair, Kristin Hilberg, Clerk Bob Stemple, Priya Sundaram, Wes Fowlks, and Sam Anderson. The Finance Committee: Chair Antony Newton, Vice-Chair, John Connor, Maria Neyland, Joe Stulpin, Michelle Ryan, and John Greven. He pointed out the Fire Station Building Committee in the front row. Moderator Reip introduced Assistant Town Administrator Rajon Hudson and Administrative Assistant, Kelley Price, running the slides. He thanked BXB-TV of Littleton Community Television for running the live stream and recording, Mark Crory, LCTV's Executive Director, LCTV’s Video Program Coordinators Judy Reid and Nicolas Casaletto. He thanked the Blanchard Memorial School principal, Michael Votto and Dan Ralls and his custodial staff and Ed Kukkula and the DPW for set up. The Boxborough Conservation Trust is hosting a refreshment table in the back. He reminded the voters about the Special Town Election on March 17, 2026 that is related to Articles 1 and 2. Moderator Reip explained the process of Town Meeting. He explained that there would be a Yes and No microphone for this town meeting. Motion on Reconsideration: Kristin Hilberg, Select Board Chair, moved and it was seconded that once final action has been taken on an Article, and the next order of business has been taken up, or the session of the Special Town Meeting has been adjourned, the Article may not again be considered at that Special Town Meeting unless the Moderator determines in his discretion that reconsideration would be in the best interest of the voters. Discussion on the motion: none Action on the motion: carried by a majority as declared by the Moderator. ARTICLE 1 PURCHASE OF PROPERTY AT 984 MASSACHUSETTS AVENUE FOR NEW FIREHOUSE $2,400,000 Bonding (Two-thirds Vote Required) Sponsor: Fire Station Building Committee Mary Brolin, Chair of the Fire Station Building Committee, moved and it was seconded that the Town vote to appropriate the sum of two million, four hundred thousand dollars ($2,400,000), to purchase, for public safety purposes including but not limited to construction of a new firehouse and all other related fire and emergency medical services or emergency management purposes, three contiguous parcels of land identified as 984 Massachusetts Avenue, Boxborough, Massachusetts, shown as Parcel ID 14-005-000 (984 Massachusetts Avenue), Parcel ID 14-003-000 (996 Massachusetts Avenue), and Parcel ID 14- 004-000 (38 Sara’s Way), and containing approximately 4.205 acres, including the payment of land acquisition costs and all other costs incidental or related thereto; that to meet this appropriation the Treasurer with the approval of the Select Board is authorized to borrow $2,400,000 under Chapter 44 of the General Laws or any other enabling authority and to issue bonds and notes of the Town 4 therefor; and, further, to authorize the Select Board to acquire the above-referenced parcels and enter into all agreements and execute any and all documents as may be necessary to effect said acquisition; provided, however, that this vote shall not take effect until the Town votes to exempt from the limitation on total taxes imposed by G.L. c.59, §21C (Proposition 2½) amounts required to pay the principal of and interest on the borrowing authorized by this vote. Summary: This article seeks Town Meeting authorization to purchase the three contiguous property lots located at 984 Massachusetts Avenue as a site for a new firehouse. The parcel allows for effective emergency response coverage and response times. The appropriation of $2,400,000 would cover the cost of the property acquisition. This article funds only the purchase of the land. A separate future Town Meeting vote would be required to fund construction of the new firehouse. The Fire Station Building Committee recommends (7-0-0). After considerable evaluation and analysis of 19 sites for viability, the Fire Station Building Committee (FSBC) is bringing forward one site for Town Meeting to vote on. The FSBC has put significant time and effort into the site selection. Overall, we evaluated 19 properties for the project. After initial assessment, we assessed five properties in depth, including 984 Massachusetts Avenue, 72 Stow Road, 1300 Massachusetts Avenue, 700-832 Massachusetts Avenue, and 502 Massachusetts Avenue, on 14 criteria including total project costs, how well the site could meet the operational needs of the fire department, the impact to abutters, and sustainability. Based on these criteria and all the data provided to us, we felt strongly that 984 Massachusetts Avenue offers the best overall solution for the Town. The 984 Massachusetts Avenue property is conveniently located on Massachusetts Avenue, is not in a residential neighborhood, has flexibility to fit the program, and is located well to serve the needs of the more densely populated areas of Town. Based on all these factors, the Fire Station Building Committee recommends this purchase. Presentation by the FSBC was given by Chair, Mary Brolin. She summarized the benefits of the site and how the site came to be available. The presentation included information about why a new firehouse is needed, the roadmap forward, and the tax impact. The timeline of the history of the firehouse was explained, starting 64 years ago. The safety, security, and non-compliance with NFPA, Building and Fire and OSHA codes were explained. She explained that the owner of 984 Mass Ave approached the Fire Chief about selling his property for the Fire House after the vote at Fall Town Meeting that allowed for zoning for this purpose. This offer was discussed with the Town Administrator and the FSBC, and a letter of intent to purchase has been signed. This agreement is good until early April, and the FSBC believes that this is a good opportunity, pending approval at Town Meeting and Special Town Election for borrowing. Ms. Brolin spoke about how the town has changed since the Fire House was built, completed in 1962. She talked about the various changes in needs and services over the past 6 decades, and how the building has not changed to keep up with those, with current hazardous and unsafe conditions for the staff. Various committees have spent almost 15 years on this initial phase of attempting to build a new Fire House. The current committee, convened in 2024, has conducted over 20 forums and public meetings. Over 20 properties have been investigated. In the fall, new sites were raised as possibilities. There were multiple rounds of assessments on several sites; in January 2026 984 Mass Ave was unanimously selected by the FSBC and supported by Finance Committee and Select Board. This site 5 avoids abutter concerns and minimizes costly legal delays and traffic concerns. She showed a map of the site and a conceptual layout of the building on the site. She described the tax impact of Article 1: starting in 2027, the tax impact would be about $76 on a $1 million house. She went on to describe the estimated construction costs at $32 million, which will be bonded over 30 years; the intent is to come back to Town Meeting next year with the actual bid in hand, with an aim to reduce the total costs during the design phase. The design and purchase costs will be wrapped into this bond. The estimate is $1,092 per year on a home value of $1 million. Because building costs escalate at least 4-5% each year, delays will cost us more. The Finance Committee recommends (6-0-0). Maria Neyland gave the Finance Committee recommendation. The Fin Com unanimously recommends this article. After years of studying multiple locations, and many opportunities for the public to comment, the Fire Station Building Committee (FSBC) has recommended 984 Massachusetts Avenue for the site of the a much-needed new fire station. The Finance Committee supports purchasing 984 Massachusetts Avenue for the new fire station. The site’s design flexibility and the early positive engagement with the abutters minimizes the risk of costly legal and construction delays. Furthermore, securing this location helps to ensure the safety and retention of firefighters by beginning to address the hazardous living /work conditions at the current station. This site deceases the risk of further project delays that would otherwise force the Town to incur the significant additional expense of providing temporary housing for our firefighting staff. For these reasons, the Finance Committee supports purchasing the 984 Massachusetts Avenue site to build a new fire station. Funding for this article will be through a short-term Bond Anticipation Note (BAN). The BAN will be refinanced into a long-term construction bond, coming for a vote in 2027. Estimated Cost to Taxpayer Land Purchase – 30 Year Bond Bond amount Annual Debt Service (Principal and Interest) Tax per $1,000 Tax per average house Assumption: Average house value Assumption: Town Value Estimated Amount $2,400,000 $148,800 $0.08 $76 $980,490 $1,915,013,882 The Select Board recommends (5-0-0). The Select Board unanimously recommends this article. Priya Sundaram gave the Select Board recommendation. The Select Board notes that Boxborough’s search for a suitable ﬁre sta on site has been ongoing for more than ﬁ een years and has involved mul ple boards and commitees. A primary challenge throughout this process has been iden fying a loca on that is centrally situated, not in a neighborhood, large enough to accommodate a modern ﬁre sta on that meets current codes and opera onal standards, and available at a reasonable cost to the Town. 6 The property at 984 Massachusets Avenue meets all of these criteria. The site is located on Massachusets Avenue with clear access and sight lines, is not situated in a neighborhood as compared to other loca ons such as Stow Road, and provides more than four acres of land, suﬃcient to support the required ﬁre sta on program. The proposed purchase price of approximately $2.4 million represents a reasonable and responsible cost for a site of this size and loca on. In addi on, this site is closer to the Town’s more densely populated areas and oﬀers improved emergency response coverage when compared to the exis ng ﬁre sta on. For these reasons, the Select Board supports the acquisi on of this property and recommends approval of this ar cle. 7 Discussion on Article 1: John Fallon of Paddock Ln thanked the many building committee members over the years for their work on this project. He emphasized the dire need for a new fire station and talked about how this site fits all of the criteria. Thomas Horsky of Depot Rd asked what the cost would be of renovating the current fire station. Mary Brolin said that the previous building committee looked into this and found that it was not feasible to renovate and it would need to be a rebuild, with an increased cost. There are severe limitations with the current site and it would have been more expensive to house the firefighters and the site has major limitations that make it challenging to meet the code and needs of the fire station. It would have been a less than optimal build for more money. Kathy Luce of Emanuel Dr said she’s fully in support of this article and spoke about how long this has been under discussion (her kids were in preschool when first starting to talk about this need and now they are in college and grad school). She asked what the next step would be if this article is not approved. Mary Brolin said that they need a new fire station and the agreement with the owner is through early April. She is not sure if he would be willing to wait; if not, the station would go to the next site under consideration which would likely be 72 Stow Rd. Having no new fire station is really not an option. Robert Hendrie of Cobleigh Rd said we are spending a lot of money in a bad economic time. He disagrees with the economics. He asked what would happen to the current fire station. Kristin Hilberg stated that that would be the purview of the select board and there are many ideas floated such as a community center, etc., and will be looking for public input when the time comes. Andrew Gruskay of Daniel’s Way asked what the Fire Chief’s opinion is of this new fire station. Chief Kivlan said they are very excited about this new site and this opportunity. Andrew Gruskay asked if there have been firefighters that have left because of the conditions. Chief Kivlan has lost about 4 firefighters in the past year and a half that have left and have said in their exit interviews that the conditions were a factor in their departure, even if not the main reason. David Rocheleau of Liberty Square Rd said that an acre of land is worth about $250-300k/acre so why would we be spending over $500k/acre? Kristin Hilberg spoke about the market value of the land and explained that the land was bought for $2.25 million in 2023 and then the lot was improved. The last lot she closed on was $450k for a single house lot. The cost is $2.4 million not $4 million. David Rocheleau asked where the property is and there was further discussion about the location. He disputed that there were more people living on the west side of town. Chief Kivlan explained that there is more density of housing units on the west side of town. Mr. Rocheleau said that brick and mortar condos would not burn, whereas houses are made of wood. Chief Kivlan reminded the speaker about the major fire on Swanson Rd at the condos several years ago. Mark Barbadoro of Old Harvard Rd commented that 20% of the town lives on the other side of 495 and that there was a disastrous fire in the condos on Swanson Rd about 5 years ago that displaced at least 8 25 families. He commended the FSBC for their plasticity in moving to this site, away from the previous site that they had chosen. He pointed out that it is mostly on lithic bedrock and that this would cause problems potentially for drainage and septic systems. He wondered if the costs of complicated septic and stormwater management systems have been accounted for in this cost. He stated that he is voting for the article regardless. Mary Brolin asked if Steve Kirby, the Owners Project Manager from Vertex could speak and Dennis Reip allowed it. Steve Kirby, the OPM, spoke about the costs included in the design budget including a possible raised septic with a pump. There is contingency money in the design costs and increased $ to address some of the complexities. There have been test pits and our resident hydrologist, Grant Garven has found that there is favorable bedrock for drilling of wells. Andew Tavolacci of Old Harvard Rd asked if Article 1 and 2 are linked. Article 2 is not contingent on a specific site? Mary Brolin said they are technically not linked. We could still vote Article 2 even if Article 1 doesn’t pass. Andrew Tavolacci asked about the need for a traffic light at 984 Mass Ave. Mary Brolin said that a traffic study was done and would not need a light, but we may do another traffic study under design just to be sure, and clarified that it would be paid for by us, working with the state. Kate Davies of Guggins Ln asked why we have to buy the land before the design is done. She is very much in support of this Article. Mary Brolin said that the design needs to be specific to the site and we need to get on the site to do all of the testing and the owner has let us on for preliminary testing but it isn’t clear if he would allow us on for further testing. There are a lot of specifics about site that will drive design and costs. Mary Nadwairski of Stonehedge Place moved the question and it was seconded. Action on the motion to stop debate: carried by 2/3s as declared by the Moderator. Action on the motion on Article 1: carried by 2/3s as declared by the Moderator. ARTICLE 2 NEW FIREHOUSE DESIGN & BID FUNDING $2,765,910 Bonding (Two-thirds Vote Required) Sponsor: Fire Station Building Committee Mary Brolin, Chair of the Fire Station Building Committee, moved and it was seconded that the Town vote to appropriate the sum of two million, seven hundred sixty-five thousand, nine hundred ten dollars ($2,765,910), to design, prepare construction drawings, pre-qualify contractors, bid the construction, and determine the lowest responsible general bid for a new firehouse, including the payment of costs incidental or related thereto; that to meet this appropriation the Treasurer with the approval of the Select Board is authorized to borrow $2,765,910 under Chapter 44 of the General Laws or any other enabling authority and to issue bonds and notes of the Town therefor; provided, however, that this vote shall not take effect until the Town votes to exempt from the limitation on total taxes imposed by G.L. c.59, §21C (Proposition 2½) amounts required to pay the principal of and interest on the borrowing authorized by this vote. 9 Summary: Over the past 20 months, the Fire Station Building Committee (FSBC) has worked closely with Vertex, our Owner’s Project Manager (OPM), and Context Architecture to review parcels of land for their feasibility to situate a new firehouse and develop the cost estimate for this article. Voting yes for this article will provide funding for the Town’s OPM, architect, and consultant team to move from conceptual design to complete design and bidding. This phase will include construction drawings with a mitigation plan, prequalification of bidders, bidding of the project, and selection of the lowest qualified general bidder. We will then come back to the voters at a future town meeting with the full, exact price to construct and deliver a new firehouse, including all furniture, fixtures, landscape, and demolition of building(s) on site. For the design and bid work, the cost is $2,765,910. The Fire Station Building Committee recommends (7-0-0). Mary Brolin gave the recommendation and presentation. After considerable evaluation and analysis of 19 sites and plans for the new firehouse, the FSBC has recommended a location for the new firehouse. The next critical step is to design the firehouse and get bids for the new firehouse so we know the actual costs. At this time, we have a conceptual estimate, but the design phase involves three interactive phases of designing the building, getting cost estimates, and value engineering to keep the building at the lowest cost possible while meeting the functional needs.
